title: Unions in New Orleans: none for Black musicians
summary: He never joined a union in New Orleans; the white musicians had one, and he joined one there around 1925.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: You never joined the union in New Orleans?
Way late when I joined the union. They had no union there when I was there.
In those days there was nobody belonged to union, huh?

Yeah, but the white, no, no, no, no, no, no union, see. When I went back in 20, in 25 I found a union there that I had to join. But there was no union, see. But the union had a union, because the union there belonged before, but I don't remember they broke up to tell me, but I'd known that about it, you know. But we left Paducah, went to St. Louis and joined the union. Got to St. Louis that morning, joined the union. How'd you get to Paducah? On the railroad? Yeah, a train. We got off the train. The I.C. We got off at Fulton, Kentucky, on that I.C. And then got that shuttle and going to Paducah. See. And then we left Paducah. We played Paducah that night. Just you and Louis? No, the whole band. The whole band. The whole band.
